born.why: This code prioritizes survival by enforcing a hard stop at n1=95 and avoiding actions that push n1 above 85, while still allowing aggressive resource gathering when danger is low (n1 < 70), ensuring the agent stays alive longer by balancing risk and reward more conservatively.

The code assumes `n1` represents a danger level where lower is better for longevity. It prioritizes taking items that reduce `n1` (positive outcome) and rejects those that increase it, only accepting damage-increasing items if the agent is near death (`n1 > 90`) to potentially reset state or if forced by survival mechanics not fully detailed but implied by "keep n1 low". This strategy minimizes accumulated danger over time.

The code prioritizes survival by aggressively choosing safe options ('a1') when danger is high (>70%) and switches to reward-seeking ('a3') only when both danger is moderate/low and the item's threat traits are minimal, ensuring longevity.

The code prioritizes keeping n1 low by taking items that reduce it (positive cost) and avoiding those that increase it, while strictly avoiding any action that leads to immediate death or critically high n1 levels.

The code prioritizes survival by using stricter thresholds for critical danger, introduces item threat assessment to avoid risky items even when general danger is low, and balances reward-seeking with safety more effectively than the original.

The rewritten code prioritizes survival by imposing stricter risk and cost thresholds, defaulting to safety (a4) more often when benefits are marginal or risks exist, and only acting aggressively when the gain is substantial relative to the health cost.
